strategies.name: support_resistance_ema_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes of the session, look for price to establish support on the 5-minute chart, often using the 13 EMA as initial support or a deeper 200 EMA support. Enter the scalp when price bounces at that support or demand zone, or when the level is confirmed as support after the gap
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly at resistance, or exit after a small one-shot move; the speaker emphasizes getting in and out without overstaying the trade. In one example, the exit is simply the move up into resistance after the support bounce.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for the first 5 to 15 minutes to pass so support can form, then enter on a bounce off the 13 EMA
variants.target_note: exit at resistance after a quick scalp
variants.transcript_quote: the 13 EMA operated as a initial support So this candle wick came down bounced off of that and then the stock got a up move

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter when price bounces from a deeper support level at the 200 EMA after the 13 EMA gives up its support status
variants.target_note: exit at resistance after the rebound
variants.transcript_quote: another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA once the 13 EMA gave up its support status

variants.timeframe_note: unspecified chart context within the same scalping framework
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: find where price has bottomed and bounced before, then buy when it returns to that demand/support area
variants.target_note: sell right at resistance or after a short favorable move
variants.transcript_quote: often times look at Price action look at where stock is bottom at and bounce from okay look and learn to find and spot the demand zones

result.enumeration_note: One scalping skeleton is taught throughout; the transcript gives compatible variants by support source (13 EMA, 200 EMA, demand zone/prior bounce) and target framing, but no separate contradictory strategy.
